care.text:
I am so deeply sorry for your loss. Losing a mother is a profound and life-altering event, and it sounds like you are carrying a heavy weight right now. It is completely understandable that you are struggling to come to terms with this; grief is not a linear journey, and there are no "right" or "wrong" ways to feel it.

The fact that you have only cried once since she passed does not mean you are not grieving. Sometimes, the mind and heart need time to process the shock before the full force of the sadness can break through. The image of your youngest daughter with your mother, holding her as a baby, is a beautiful anchor. It is wonderful that you are finding comfort in that memory. It seems like your heart is trying to protect you by focusing on the love and connection you shared, rather than the trauma of the final moments. That is a natural and healthy way to cope.

It is okay to hold onto the memory of her as a grandmother and a mother, and it is also okay to feel the pain of how she left. You don't have to choose one over the other. If the memories of her final moments feel too heavy or intrusive, try to gently remind yourself of the love she gave you and your daughter.

Please be gentle with yourself. You are allowed to take all the time you need to heal. If you ever feel overwhelmed or just need to talk about the good memories, or even the hard ones, I am here to listen without judgment. You are not alone in this.

It is completely understandable that you are struggling to come to terms with this; grief is not a linear journey, and there are no "right" or "wrong" ways to feel it.

Sometimes, the mind and heart need time to process the shock before the full force of the sadness can break through. The image of your youngest daughter with your mother, holding her as a baby, is a beautiful anchor. It is wonderful that you are finding comfort in that memory. It seems like your heart is trying to protect you by focusing on the love and connection you shared, rather than the trauma of the final moments. That is a natural and healthy way to cope.

It is okay to hold onto the memory of her as a grandmother and a mother, and it is also okay to feel the pain of how she left. You don't have to choose one over the other. If the memories of her final moments feel too heavy or intrusive, try to gently remind yourself of the love she gave you and your daughter.

Please be gentle with yourself. You are allowed to take all the time you need to heal. If you ever feel overwhelmed or just need to talk about the good memories, or even the hard ones, I am here to listen without judgment. You are not alone in this.
